description: How SAS regression procedures detect collinearity and rank via a relative pivot tolerance on the crossproduct matrix (SINGULAR=), and why this differs from numpy's SVD rank.

relative_pivot_tolerance.title: SAS aliases a column when its crossproduct pivot falls below SINGULAR x its original diagonal (relative, not absolute).
rule: SAS regression forms the crossproduct matrix X'X and sweeps it column by column (in model order).

A column is declared linearly dependent ('aliased') when, after removing the variance explained by the columns already in the model, its remaining pivot is below SINGULAR x (its original X'X diagonal).
The comparison is RELATIVE to the original diagonal, so it is scale-aware; it is not an absolute threshold.
Default SINGULAR is small (PROC REG uses 1E-7; other procs are similar). Match the baseline's option when known.
Aliased columns get a zero (or missing) coefficient and do NOT consume a degree of freedom; model rank = number of non-aliased columns.
This matters for reproducing SAS: numpy.linalg.matrix_rank uses an SVD/absolute tolerance and can report a different rank for near-collinear designs, changing df, RMSE, and which variables survive.
pitfalls: Do not rely on np.linalg.matrix_rank for SAS parity on near-collinear data; it can keep a column SAS would alias.
Squaring X into X'X squares the condition number; if numerical stability is a concern, apply the same relative-tolerance logic directly on X's columns via sequential projection.
Column order matters: SAS aliases the LATER of two collinear columns because it sweeps in model order.

code: """Rank of a design matrix using SAS-style relative pivot tolerance on X'X."""
diag0 = np.diag(A).copy()          # original diagonals = per-column reference scale
rank += 1                  # independent -> eliminate below the pivot
A[i + 1:, i:] -= np.outer(A[i + 1:, i] / A[i, i], A[i, i:])

reference_impl.note: Sequential-projection variant of the same relative-tolerance rank, used for GLMSELECT selection/aliasing; see also SAS2PY/semantic_layer/reference/generic/matrix_rank.py.
